description: Observe the Great Conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn on December 21, 2020 — the closest conjunction of these two planets since 1623. Set the observer location to Paranal Observatory, Chile (24.6272° S, 70.4042° W, altitude 2635m) and navigate to the correct date and time (approximately 18:00 UTC) when the conjunction was visible after sunset. Find Jupiter and Saturn in the sky, center the view on them, and zoom in until both planets and their moons are clearly visible in a single field of view.

metadata.event_name: Great Conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn
